unit.title: Sequence of Tenses
unit.subtitle: Matching the subjunctive to your main verb

grammar.title: The main verb decides which subjunctive you use
grammar.intro: Once a verb triggers the subjunctive, you still have to pick the right tense. Spanish settles this with the correlación de tiempos (sequence of tenses): the tense of the main verb tells you whether to reach for a present-side or a past-side subjunctive. Get the pairing right and everything else falls into place.

sections.heading: Present / future / command → present-side subjunctive
sections.body: If the main verb is present, future, or a command, use the present subjunctive (simultaneous/future action) or the present-perfect subjunctive (already completed):

ex.en: I hope you have come early.

sections.heading: Past / conditional → past-side subjunctive
sections.body: If the main verb is past (preterite, imperfect) or conditional, use the imperfect subjunctive (simultaneous/later) or the pluperfect subjunctive (already completed):

ex.en: I was hoping you would come.
I would like you to come.

sections.heading: Same verb, shifted in time
sections.body: The cleanest way to feel the rule is to shift one sentence from present to past. The trigger verb stays the same; both halves slide back together:

ex.es: Dudo que sea verdad. → Dudaba que fuera verdad.
ex.en: I doubt it's true. → I doubted it was true.
I want you to study. → I wanted you to study.

takeaways: Present / future / command main verb → present or present-perfect subjunctive.
Past / conditional main verb → imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive.
Quiero que estudies vs. Quería que estudiaras.
Conditional counts as past-side: Me gustaría que vinieras.

mistakes.why: A past main verb (quería) needs a past-side subjunctive: estudiaras, not estudies.
The conditional (me gustaría) is past-side, so it takes the imperfect subjunctive: vinieras.
After the imperfect dudaba, use the imperfect subjunctive fuera, not the present sea.

exercises.prompt_en: I wanted you to study more.
exercises.no: A past main verb (quería) needs the imperfect subjunctive: “estudiaras”.
A present main verb (espero) takes the present subjunctive: “vengas”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I would like you to come with me.”
exercises.no: “Me gustaría que vinieras conmigo” — the conditional is past-side, so use vinieras.

exercises.hint: Past main verb → imperfect subjunctive of ser.
exercises.no: After the past 'dudaba', use the imperfect subjunctive: “fuera”.

exercises.prompt: Match each main verb to the subjunctive tense it triggers.

exercises.translation: I wanted you to study more.
exercises.no: It was: “Quería que estudiaras más.” (I wanted you to study more.)

exercises.scenario: A manager recalls last month's request 📋

lines.speaker: Jefe
lines.es: El mes pasado te pedí un cambio en el informe.
lines.en: Last month I asked you for a change in the report.

options.text: Sí, quería que añadiera los gráficos.
Sí, quería que añada los gráficos.
Sí, quería que añado los gráficos.

exercises.no: A past main verb (quería) needs the imperfect subjunctive: “que añadiera”.

exercises.en: I would like you to come with me.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “Me gustaría que vinieras conmigo.”
